mechanism: A self-amending governance protocol where rejected amendment attempts that pass basic validation but fail at {{quorum}} trigger an automatic Immunization Event. The system analyzes the structural logic of the failed proposal and generates a new Antibody Rule that explicitly forbids that class of logic in future proposals. Consequently, an attacker who crafts sophisticated edge-case attacks is training the system's immune system, progressively narrowing the space of possible exploits. It requires a {{quorum}} failure to trigger the immune response, codifying the rejected attack vector into a new law. Proposals that fail basic schema validation (spam) do NOT trigger immunization—only proposals sophisticated enough to reach governance review.
gloss: Governance that hardens through failed attacks
failure_modes: Ossification (the system accumulates so many immunities that it becomes unable to pass legitimate, necessary changes).
Spam-triggered bloat: if severity threshold is set too low, low-quality rejections generate useless antibodies.
invariants: Antifragile Hardening: Cost(Attack N+1) > Cost(Attack N)
Monotonic Safety: The set of forbidden transitions can only grow (within decay window)
preconditions: Proposal P passed basic schema validation (is not trivial spam)

parameters.name: severity_floor
parameters.description: Minimum threat score for a rejection to trigger antibody generation
